name: Naivedyam
instructions: 1. Roast the gram flour in pure ghee over low heat until it turns golden brown and aromatic.
2. In a separate pan, prepare a sugar syrup of one-string consistency.
3. Add the roasted flour to the sugar syrup, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
4. Incorporate chopped cashews, almonds, raisins, cardamom powder, and a tiny pinch of edible camphor.
5. Once the mixture cools slightly, grease your palms with ghee and shape the mixture into firm, round laddus while warm.
description: Naivedyam is famously associated with the Mahavir Mandir in Patna, Bihar. It is a traditional sweet offered to Lord Hanuman. The dish is unique for its distinctive aroma of edible camphor and its rich, ghee-laden texture, symbolizing purity and devotion.
